instructions_en: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Raise the dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower them slowly without swinging your body.
Stand side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in the far hand.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height, leading with the elbow.
Lower it slowly and keep your torso still.
Sit with your shoulders lined up with the machine's pivot and the pads against your outer arms.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower them under control to the start.
Stand between two low pulleys and cross the cables so each hand holds the opposite handle.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y shape, thumbs slightly up.
Lower them slowly without shrugging.
Hold the loaded end of a landmine bar at shoulder height, feet staggered.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it back to your shoulder under control.
Hinge until your torso is about parallel to the floor and take an overhand grip on a barbell resting on the floor.
Pull the bar hard to your lower chest while your back stays flat.
Return the bar to the floor and reset before the next rep.
Lie face down on a raised flat bench with a barbell on the floor below you.
Pull the bar to the underside of the bench, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it until your arms are straight.
Stand side-on to the loaded end of a landmine bar in a staggered stance and grip the end of the bar with one hand.
Row the bar toward your hip while your torso stays still.
Lower it until your arm is straight, finish the set, then switch sides.
Stand facing away from a low pulley with the handle in one hand, arm slightly behind your body.
Curl the handle up while your upper arm stays still.
Lower it slowly until your arm is straight behind you.
Stand on one leg with a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip and let the free leg travel back until you feel a stretch in the standing leg's hamstring.
Drive the hip forward to stand tall.
Pick up a heavy dumbbell in one hand.
Walk tall without leaning toward or away from the weight.
Switch hands for the next set.
Lie on your side and prop yourself up on your forearm, elbow under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold the position, then switch sides.
Lie on your back with your arms overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs a few inches off it.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Start on your hands and knees with a flat back.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Return and repeat on the other side without rotating your hips.
Lie on your side with your top leg resting on a bench and your forearm on the floor.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line, supported by the top leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
Sit with the handles at mid-chest height and your back against the pad.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Sit facing the pec deck pad with the handles set in front of you at shoulder height.
Sweep your arms back and out in a wide arc, leading with the elbows.
Return slowly to the start.
Set both pulleys low and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Sweep your arms up and together in front of your upper chest.
Lower them slowly to the start with a slight bend in the elbows.
Set both pulleys high and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Sweep your arms down and together in front of your lower chest.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Set up as for a bench press.
Lower the bar and stop it about an inch above your chest, holding it there briefly.
Press it back up without letting it touch your chest.
Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a barbell held at shoulder height.
Press the bar overhead while your torso stays upright.
Lower it back to your shoulders under control.
Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a dumbbell at each shoulder.
Press the dumbbells overhead without leaning back.
Lower them back to your shoulders under control.
Hold a sturdy upright with one hand and lean away from it, a dumbbell in the other hand.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower it slowly, finish the set, then switch sides.
Lie face down on the chest pad of a T-bar row and grip the handles.
Row the handles toward your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower them until your arms are straight.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the handles with straight arms.
Pull the handles toward your torso, driving your elbows back.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the low handles.
Pull the handles toward your hips with your elbows close to your body.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grip one handle.
Row the handle toward your side, driving your elbow back.
Return slowly, finish the set, then switch arms.
Sit at a lat pulldown and grip the bar with your palms facing you, about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let it rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Brace one hand on a bench or rack, a heavy dumbbell in the other hand.
Row the dumbbell toward your hip, letting your torso move a little near the top.
Lower it all the way for a full stretch; sets are usually high reps.
Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, torso leaned forward about 30 degrees.
Pull the bar to your lower stomach, driving your elbows back.
Lower it until your arms are straight.
Stand at a Smith machine holding the bar at hip height, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the bar along your thighs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Set the pad just below your hips on a 45-degree back extension bench and anchor your feet.
Lower your torso by hinging at the hips while your back stays flat.
Raise it until your body forms a straight line.
Stand on the platform with your back against the pad and your shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Squat down as deep as you can control, heels on the platform.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.
Stand on the platform with your shoulders under the pads and your back against the support.
Bend your knees and lower yourself until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Push through your feet to return to the top.
Set up as for a back squat.
Squat to the bottom and hold still for about two seconds.
Drive back up without bouncing.
Stand with your heels on a small plate or wedge, holding a dumbbell at your chest.
Squat down with your torso upright, letting your knees travel forward.
Stand back up through your whole foot.
Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and stand side-on with the strap on your outer ankle.
Lift the leg out to the side without leaning your torso.
Lower it slowly, finish the set, then switch legs.
